hero.description: The platform combines GTD, GUT, MASP and PDCA to turn loose inputs into execution guided by priority, analysis and continuous improvement.

gtd.title: GTD
gtd.what: Captures and organizes everything that enters the system.
gtd.how: Turns loose pending items into reliable next actions and reviews.

gut.title: GUT
gut.what: Prioritizes by severity, urgency and trend.
gut.how: Distinguishes what needs an immediate response from what can wait.

masp.title: MASP
masp.how: Moves from root cause identification to standardized learning.

pdca.title: PDCA
pdca.how: Plans, executes, checks and adjusts the operation on every iteration.

gtdSection.title: Clarity before execution.
gtdSection.description: GTD works as an operational trust layer: everything can be captured, clarified and repositioned without depending on the user's memory.

gtdSteps.title: Capture
gtdSteps.what: Register demands, ideas and interruptions as soon as they appear.
gtdSteps.how: The initial backlog absorbs inputs without forcing an immediate decision.

gtdSteps.title: Clarify
gtdSteps.what: Understand whether the input requires action, reference or disposal.
gtdSteps.how: Each item receives context, action type and next step.

gtdSteps.title: Organize
gtdSteps.what: Place the information in the correct system structure.
gtdSteps.how: Categories, projects, boxes and states avoid operational ambiguity.

gtdSteps.title: Reflect
gtdSteps.what: Review the flow to keep the system reliable.
gtdSteps.how: Reviews verify priorities, pending items and deviations.

gtdSteps.title: Engage
gtdSteps.what: Execute with focus on what makes the most sense now.
gtdSteps.how: Prioritization guides the choice of the next action.

gutSection.title: Criteria for decisions under pressure.
gutSection.description: Severity, urgency and trend become a common language to order the backlog and avoid decisions driven only by impulse.

gutFactors.title: Severity
gutFactors.what: Measures the real impact if nothing is done.
gutFactors.how: Considers operational damage, risk and effect on outcomes.

gutFactors.title: Urgency
gutFactors.how: Brings time directly into the prioritization decision.

gutFactors.title: Trend
gutFactors.what: Measures the chance of the problem getting worse.
gutFactors.how: Helps anticipate bottlenecks before they become a crisis.

maspSection.title: Problems treated with method.
maspSection.description: MASP organizes analysis, action and verification so the operation does not just react, but learns from every deviation.

maspSteps.title: Identification
maspSteps.how: Delimits scope, impact and context before acting.

maspSteps.title: Observation
maspSteps.what: Gather data from the problem in the real environment.
maspSteps.how: Collects signals, recurrences and associated conditions.

maspSteps.title: Analysis
maspSteps.what: Investigate likely causes and origin relationships.
maspSteps.how: Separates symptom from root cause to avoid rework.

maspSteps.title: Action plan
maspSteps.what: Define the structured response for correction.
maspSteps.how: Organizes owners, deadlines and execution strategy.

maspSteps.title: Execution
maspSteps.what: Apply the actions defined in the plan.
maspSteps.how: Moves the issue from diagnosis to real intervention.

maspSteps.title: Verification
maspSteps.what: Check whether the expected effect happened.
maspSteps.how: Compares before and after to validate the result.

maspSteps.title: Standardization
maspSteps.how: Prevents the same cause from reappearing in the flow.

maspSteps.title: Conclusion
maspSteps.what: Record the learning and close the cycle.
maspSteps.how: Ends the trail with documentation and future reference.

pdcaSection.title: The cycle that keeps operations evolving.

pdcaPhases.title: PLAN
pdcaPhases.what: Plan the path and success criteria.
pdcaPhases.how: Defines objective, scope and how delivery will be validated.

pdcaPhases.title: DO
pdcaPhases.what: Execute the plan in the operational flow.

pdcaPhases.title: CHECK
pdcaPhases.how: Checks whether execution matches the plan.

pdcaPhases.title: ACT
pdcaPhases.what: Act on learnings and required adjustments.
pdcaPhases.how: Standardizes improvements and repositions the next cycle.

paragraphs: We were not designed for the information age. Our biological hardware evolved to handle immediate threats and tangible rewards.
Today we operate in an environment of infinite inputs. The result is cognitive anxiety, mental loops and an overloaded operating system.
hero.quote: The mind is for having ideas, not holding them.

gut.description: When everything feels urgent, the answer is not intuition. The GUT matrix decomposes chaos into measurable vectors that guide priority.

cards.title: Severity
cards.description: Impact if nothing is done. Damage, losses and system collapse.

cards.title: Urgency
cards.description: Available time for resolution. Is the deadline expiring now?

cards.title: Trend
cards.description: Potential growth of the problem. Will it worsen progressively?

paragraphs: Getting Things Done (GTD) is not about doing more. It is about building a proportional response state for every new input.
When you trust the system, the brain stops spending RAM trying to remember pending items and starts operating strategy.
algorithmSteps: ORGANIZE: Put it in the right place.

paragraphs: The human brain processes images much faster than text. Kanban turns abstract work into visual objects moving through space.
Limiting WIP (Work In Progress) is the only way to avoid bottlenecks. If everything is a priority, nothing is a priority.
Efficiency is not monolithic. It emerges from the balance between cognitive load and throughput.
Visual systems reduce immediate anxiety, while structured list-based systems maximize long-term retrieval accuracy.
analysis.tableSubtitle: LIVE DATA FEED • REAL-TIME COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS
analysis.closing: Kanban, highlighted above, optimizes flow visibility, but often sacrifices the capture of granular details.

final.title: FINAL_OUTPUT //
final.tipText: To sell this methodology to stakeholders, emphasize 'Risk Reduction' (MASP) instead of 'Speed' (Kanban).
